\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =\begin{vmatrix}3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & -1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =3\cdot \begin{vmatrix}2 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{vmatrix}-0\cdot \begin{vmatrix}0 & 2 \\ 3 & -1\end{vmatrix}+(-1)\cdot \begin{vmatrix}0 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =3(2\cdot (-1)-2\cdot 1)-0+(-1)(0\cdot 1-2\cdot 3) \\  & =3(-2-2)+6 \\  & =-12+6 \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|-6|=6.
$$

problem:
Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{AC}$, and $\overrightarrow{AD}$, given

$$
A(3,1,1),\quad B(1,1,1),\quad C(4,4,1),\quad D(3,2,3).
$$

First subtract the coordinates of $A$ from each endpoint to find the three edge vectors. Then use

$$
V=\left|\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot\left(\overrightarrow{AC}\times\overrightarrow{AD}\right)\right|.
$$

The schematic shows the three edges meeting at a common vertex, with $\mathbf{a}=\overrightarrow{AB}$, $\mathbf{b}=\overrightarrow{AC}$, and $\mathbf{c}=\overrightarrow{AD}$.

![](images/25/2597b48a010607fca71c551dbce8e9e2bbeda47d0892a582347ae1cdf19f1bf6.png)

Select the volume in cubic units.
solution:
Form each displacement vector by subtracting the common starting point $A$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{AB}&=\langle 1-3,1-1,1-1\rangle=\langle-2,0,0\rangle,\\
\overrightarrow{AC}&=\langle 4-3,4-1,1-1\rangle=\langle1,3,0\rangle,\\
\overrightarrow{AD}&=\langle 3-3,2-1,3-1\rangle=\langle0,1,2\rangle.
\end{aligned}
$$

The scalar triple product is the determinant with these edge vectors as rows. Expanding along the first row, the two zero entries leave just one term:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot(\overrightarrow{AC}\times\overrightarrow{AD})
&=\begin{vmatrix}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{vmatrix}\\
&=(-2)\begin{vmatrix}3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{vmatrix}\\
&=(-2)(3\cdot2-0\cdot1)\\
&=-12.
\end{aligned}
$$

Volume is the absolute value of the triple product, so

$$
V=|-12|=12\text{ cubic units}.
$$

The negative triple product describes orientation; it does not give a negative volume. Using the position vectors of $B$, $C$, and $D$ without subtracting $A$ would give the wrong edges.

problem:
Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{AC}$, and $\overrightarrow{AD}$, given

$$
A(1,-1,2),\quad B(2,1,2),\quad C(0,0,4),\quad D(3,-1,3).
$$

Select the volume in cubic units.
solution:
First find the displacement vectors from the common vertex $A$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{AB}&=\langle2-1,1-(-1),2-2\rangle=\langle1,2,0\rangle,\\
\overrightarrow{AC}&=\langle0-1,0-(-1),4-2\rangle=\langle-1,1,2\rangle,\\
\overrightarrow{AD}&=\langle3-1,-1-(-1),3-2\rangle=\langle2,0,1\rangle.
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $T=\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot(\overrightarrow{AC}\times\overrightarrow{AD})$. Expand its determinant along the first row. The cofactor signs are $+,-,+$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
T&=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}\\
&=1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}-2\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{vmatrix}+0\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{vmatrix}\\
&=1(1\cdot1-2\cdot0)-2((-1)\cdot1-2\cdot2)+0\\
&=1-2(-5)\\
&=11.
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
V=|11|=11\text{ cubic units}.
$$

Both nonzero cofactor contributions are needed. The middle contribution is positive because the cofactor sign and its minor are both negative. There is no division by six: that factor would give a tetrahedron's volume.

problem:
Calculate the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{AC}$, and $\overrightarrow{AD}$, given

$$
A(-1,2,-1),\quad B(1,1,0),\quad C(0,3,0),\quad D(0,4,-3).
$$

Enter the volume in cubic units.

$V=$ {{field-1}}
solution:
Subtract $A$ from each endpoint to obtain the three edge vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{AB}&=\langle1-(-1),1-2,0-(-1)\rangle=\langle2,-1,1\rangle,\\
\overrightarrow{AC}&=\langle0-(-1),3-2,0-(-1)\rangle=\langle1,1,1\rangle,\\
\overrightarrow{AD}&=\langle0-(-1),4-2,-3-(-1)\rangle=\langle1,2,-2\rangle.
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $T=\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot(\overrightarrow{AC}\times\overrightarrow{AD})$. All three first-row cofactor contributions are nonzero:

$$
\begin{aligned}
T&=\begin{vmatrix}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & -2\end{vmatrix}\\
&=2\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -2\end{vmatrix}-(-1)\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{vmatrix}+1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{vmatrix}\\
&=2(1\cdot(-2)-1\cdot2)\\
&\quad{}-(-1)(1\cdot(-2)-1\cdot1)\\
&\quad{}+1(1\cdot2-1\cdot1)\\
&=2(-4)+(-3)+1\\
&=-8-3+1\\
&=-10.
\end{aligned}
$$

The required volume is the absolute value:

$$
V=|-10|=10\text{ cubic units}.
$$

Using the endpoint position vectors instead of the displacement vectors changes the solid. Taking the absolute value of each cofactor term separately is also incorrect: combine the signed contributions before taking the absolute value.
